GAAP net loss for Q4 2025 was $100.1 million and for full year 2025 was $435.1 million.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA loss was $252.3 million, representing approximately a 10% year-over-year improvement from $285 million in 2024.
For 2026, QuantumScape expects full year adjusted EBITDA loss to be between $250 million and $275 million.
Full year 2025 capital expenditures were $36.3 million, and 2026 CapEx is expected to be between $40 million and $60 million, with the bulk directed toward going beyond the QSE-5 platform.
Customer billings for full year 2025 totaled $19.5 million, with the full amount received in cash during Q4 and recorded directly to shareholders' equity due to related-party accounting requirements.
QuantumScape ended 2025 with $970.8 million in liquidity.

In 2025, QuantumScape added two major global automotive OEMs to its customer portfolio through new joint development and technology evaluation agreements, in addition to expanding its collaboration and licensing agreement with PowerCo/Volkswagen Group.

The expanded PowerCo collaboration agreement includes an opportunity to earn up to $131 million in development-type payments, and the $150 million-plus conditional cash inflow figure reflects billings to date plus a $130 million prepaid, with no contractual changes from prior disclosures.
QuantumScape expects customer billings in 2026 to increase relative to 2025 levels as it deepens and expands customer engagements.
QuantumScape added Murata Manufacturing and Corning as ceramic production partners to its ecosystem, with Murata and Corning taking over manufacturing of the ceramic separator.
Total revenue for Q3 2025 was $70.8 million compared to $138.7 million in Q3 2024, with the decline entirely due to the sunset of migrant-related projects.
Excluding migrant-related programs, base business revenue increased 8% year-over-year to $62.4 million in Q3 2025 from $58 million in Q3 2024.
The company issued 2026 guidance of $280 million to $300 million in revenue, representing 12% to 20% year-over-year base business growth, with adjusted EBITDA loss of $15 million to $25 million.
Medical Transportation business is expected to generate more than $200 million of revenue in 2025 and achieved record volumes in Q3.
The company assigned over 26,000 trips to other vendors over the last 12 months due to capacity constraints and plans to hire 700 to 800 additional EMS staff to capture this embedded demand.
SteadyMD acquisition adds a 50-state virtual care network with over 500 clinicians, projected to generate approximately $25 million in revenue in 2025 and service over 3 million patients.
Remote patient monitoring is operating at an annual run rate of approximately $15 million with greater than 10% adjusted EBITDA contribution margin.
The company paid off the $30 million outstanding balance on its credit line during Q3, making the balance sheet debt-free for the first time since late 2023.
Total cash and cash equivalents, including restricted cash and investments, was $95.2 million as of September 30, 2025, with expected exit cash of approximately $65 million at the end of 2026.
The company has collected approximately 96% of all migrant-related receivables from inception, with approximately $37 million remaining at quarter end compared to $150 million at the end of 2024.
Q1 2026 revenue was $170.9 million, up 42% year-over-year and 17% sequentially, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.41 growing over 80% year-over-year and 30% sequentially, above the high end of guidance.

Lattice announced a definitive agreement to acquire AMI for $1.65 billion ($1 billion cash and $650 million equity, ~5.4 million shares based on May 1 closing price), expected to close in Q3 and be immediately accretive to gross margin, free cash flow, and non-GAAP EPS.

Combined with AMI, Lattice expects to exceed a $1 billion annual revenue run rate by the end of 2026 with roughly 40% free cash flow margin, and management expects the SAM to roughly double from ~$6 billion to ~$12 billion over the next 3-4 years.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $175-$195 million (midpoint ~$185M, nearly 50% YoY growth) and non-GAAP EPS of $0.42-$0.46 (midpoint ~80% YoY growth), with gross margin of 70% ±1% and OpEx of $64-$67 million.

Compute and Communications revenue grew 86% year-over-year and 15% sequentially, reached a record, and represented 62% of Q1 revenue, while Industrial and Embedded grew 21% sequentially and 10% year-over-year.

Server revenue is expected to rise to about 38% of total revenue in 2026 (up from teens a couple of years ago), and AI-related revenue is expected to reach about 25% in 2026, up from high-teens in 2025 and mid-teens in 2024.
Channel inventory dropped from 3 months last quarter to close to 2 months, with expectations to fall below 2 months in Q2; management noted backlog and bookings now extend well into 2027.
Q1 non-GAAP gross margin was 70% (up 60 bps QoQ, 100 bps YoY), operating margin expanded 370 bps to 34.4%, and EBITDA margin rose 310 bps to 39.6%.

Q1 GAAP operating cash flow was $50.3 million (down from $57.6M in Q4) and free cash flow was $39.7 million (down from $44M), with $15 million in share repurchases and the quarter ending with $140 million in cash and no debt.

Lattice models ~16.5 million servers in 2026 with roughly 3 FPGAs per server and rising ASPs, while THL Partners' $650M equity stake will be locked up for 12 months post-close, releasing 25% per quarter.
Adjusting for assumption changes and charges, core EPS was $0.29 for the quarter, with Q4 guidance of $0.30 to $0.35 per share.
Navient announced a new share repurchase authorization of $100 million.

For the third straight quarter, Earnest doubled origination volume year-over-year, totaling approximately $800 million in new loans including $528 million in refi loans (highest quarterly volume this year) and a record $260 million in in-school lending.
The company raised full-year total loan originations guidance to around $2.4 billion, over 30% higher than guidance provided at the beginning of the year.

Expected life of loan cash flows increased by approximately $195 million due to lower prepayment speeds, with prepayment assumption changes alone increasing expected future cash flows by approximately $280 million.
Revised default and post-default recovery assumptions increased expected net life of loan charge-offs by $151 million, which is reflected as provision expense in Q3 results.

Total core operating expenses for the quarter declined by $93 million to $109 million compared to a year ago, and the company is on track to remove over 90% of its $400 million run-rate expense reduction target by the end of 2025.
FFELP prepayment rate assumptions were lowered from 5% CPR to 3%, and private legacy portfolio CPR was lowered from 10% to 8%.
The company returned $42 million to shareholders through share repurchases (2 million shares at an average price of $13.19) and dividends while maintaining an adjusted tangible equity ratio of 9.3%.
Year-to-date, Navient has issued nearly $2.2 billion of term ABS financing across four securitizations with strong investor demand and high advance rates.
Q1 2026 consolidated revenue increased 1.3% year-over-year to $849 million, with organic revenue growth of 1%, while adjusted EBITDA rose $3 million to $244 million with margin up 10 basis points.

Adjusted diluted EPS was $2.50 versus $2.33 in Q1 2025, a 7% increase, and the company raised its full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.00-$4.10 assuming approximately 60.5 million weighted average fully diluted shares.

CBIZ reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $2.8-$2.9 billion (2%-5% growth) and free cash flow of $270-$290 million, while updating adjusted EBITDA range to $465-$475 million for stock-based compensation adjustments.

Management estimates transitory client attrition and integration-related productivity impacts reduced Q1 reported organic revenue growth by approximately 200 basis points, and excluding these, Financial Services organic growth would have been approximately 4% versus the reported 1.8%.

Benefits and Insurance revenue declined 4% year-over-year to $108 million in Q1, hurt by tough project/contingent commission comps and the unexpected February departure of a single producer and his team, though the recurring portion normalized for that departure grew approximately 4%.

Net leverage improved to approximately 3.4x from 3.9x a year ago, with a long-term target of less than 2.5x by 2027, supported by free cash flow that improved $64 million year-over-year (aided by a $53 million one-time purchase price adjustment).

The company repurchased approximately 2 million shares for roughly $63 million through April and signaled it will remain active and opportunistic given its view that the stock is undervalued and buybacks are highly accretive.
Offshore hours are on track to increase from approximately 6% in 2025 to 10% in 2026, with a multi-year plan to exceed 20% to drive significant margin and growth opportunities.

AI-based data extraction in one attest service is producing 20% efficiency in year one, with expectations to grow to 40% efficiency in subsequent years, as CBIZ transitions from AI-assisted to agentic AI workflows company-wide post-busy season.

Management is targeting an approximately 15% full-year increase in Benefits and Insurance producers, mid-single-digit pricing increases, and expects organic growth to accelerate each quarter to exit 2026 at the mid-single-digit target rate.
Q1 2026 total revenue grew 79% year-over-year to $216 million, with molecular profiling services revenue up 85% to $211 million.
GAAP gross margin expanded to 65% from 47% in Q1 2025, an improvement of over 1,800 basis points year-over-year.
Caris delivered positive adjusted EBITDA of $26 million and positive free cash flow of $22.5 million, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of both, with cash growing to over $825 million.
Clinical case volumes rose 15% year-over-year to approximately 52,800 (43,600 tissue and 9,200 Caris Assure), with tissue ASP up 70% to over $4,300 and blood ASP up 14% to just under $2,500.

Management guided to roughly 58,000 completed cases in Q2 (a 10% sequential volume increase) and a Q2 revenue growth of approximately 32%, while reaffirming full-year guidance of low-teens tissue growth and high-50s to low-60s blood growth.
The Achieve 1 final readout for Caris Detect MCED showed 60.3% Stage I/II sensitivity and 99.2% asymptomatic specificity across 3,014 subjects, with commercial launch planned in Q2 via Everlywell.
Caris ChromoSeq was launched April 1 with MolDX approval at a price of $3,228, addressing approximately 50,000 patients across AML, MDS and MPN indications.

The sales force was expanded from 82 to 146 territories with over 270 commercial team members (targeting ~300), driving February-March activations up ~20% year-over-year and full-quarter activations up 17%.

Caris refinanced into a new $400 million debt facility led by Blue Owl and Blackstone, saving ~$6 million in annual interest, extending maturity from January 2028 to April 2031, and adding a $300 million delayed draw term loan for potential M&A.

Caris submitted its PAMA data on May 1 for both CDLT-classified assays and does not expect any downward pricing adjustments, with MI Cancer Seek covered lives now above $225 million and representing more than 75% of Q1 tissue volume.

Elevance Health established 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance of at least $25.50, compared to full year 2025 adjusted diluted EPS of $30.29 which included approximately $3.75 per share of favorable nonrecurring items.
The company expects to return to at least 12% adjusted EPS growth in 2027 off the ending 2026 earnings baseline.
Medicare Advantage membership is expected to decline in the high teens percentage range in 2026, reflecting deliberate portfolio actions and geographic exits.
Medicaid operating margin is expected to be approximately negative 1.75% in 2026, with management viewing 2026 as the trough year for Medicaid.
Operating cash flow for 2025 was $4.3 billion (approximately 0.8x GAAP net income), with 2026 operating cash flow expected to be at least $5.5 billion.
The company returned $4.1 billion of capital to shareholders in 2025, including $2.6 billion in share repurchases and plans to allocate approximately $2.3 billion towards share repurchases in 2026.
Long-term enterprise margin target was revised to 5% to 6%, with Health Benefits, Carelon and CarelonRx now targeting mid-single-digit margins.
Medicare Advantage operating margin is expected to improve by more than 100 basis points to at least 2% in 2026.
Fourth quarter 2025 operating revenue totaled $49.3 billion, an increase of 10% from the prior year.
Medicaid membership is expected to decline approximately 750,000 members in 2026 due to continued eligibility reverification requirements and more stringent state eligibility standards.
ADP reported Q1 fiscal 2026 revenue growth of 7% and adjusted EPS growth of 7%.
Employer Services new business bookings resulted in a record sales volume for the first quarter, with growth accelerating from Q4 of last year.
Employer Services pays per control growth rounded down to 0% for Q1 and is now forecast to remain approximately flat for the full year, down from the prior 0% to 1% range.
More than 80% of new mid-market clients in the 50 to 150 employee space were sold on the Next Gen version of Workforce Now in Q1.

ADP increased its full year client funds interest revenue forecast by $10 million to a range of $1.30 billion to $1.32 billion, driven by stronger average client funds balance growth now expected at 3% to 4%.
PEO revenue growth of 7% exceeded expectations, with average worksite employee growth of 2% in the quarter.
Employer Services margin decreased 50 basis points in Q1 due to integration and acquisition-related costs from the WorkForce Software acquisition.
PEO margin decreased 140 basis points in Q1, mainly driven by higher selling expenses, timing of state unemployment insurance costs, and zero-margin pass-through revenue growth.
ADP Assist recorded more than 5.5 million client conversations over the last year.
ADP is maintaining its fiscal 2026 guidance for 5% to 6% consolidated revenue growth, 50 to 70 basis points adjusted EBIT margin expansion, and 8% to 10% adjusted EPS growth.
MicroVision reported Q4 2025 revenue of $0.2 million, down from $1.7 million in Q4 2024, and full year 2025 revenue of $1.2 million, down from $4.7 million in 2024.
The company provided 2026 revenue guidance of $10 million to $15 million, based on prior MicroVision outlook and continuing Luminar revenue streams.

Cash used in operations plus CapEx for 2026 is expected to be in the range of $65 million to $70 million, a modest increase over 2025 due primarily to the acquisitions of Scantinel, Luminar, and the addition of the Virginia-based aerial systems team.
At the end of Q4 2025, MicroVision had $74.8 million in cash, cash equivalents, and investment securities, plus $43 million available under the current ATM facility.

Subsequent to year-end, MicroVision issued two new senior secured convertible notes totaling $43 million in aggregate principal, of which $19.5 million will repay the current outstanding note balance and interest, with the remainder available for general operations.
Full year 2025 cash-based operating expenses were $45.5 million, a decline of $14.4 million or 24% compared to full year 2024, driven by reduced purchased services and headcount reductions.

The company recorded $29.4 million of noncash asset impairment and adverse purchase commitment charges in Q4, including $16 million related to MOVIA L inventory and $13.4 million primarily attributed to perception software and MAVIN equipment.

MicroVision anticipates additional asset impairment charges of $8 million to $12 million related to its Redmond office lease and $1 million to $2 million in people-related restructuring charges from consolidating operations into Orlando.
The Luminar acquisition brought approximately 30 new customer relationships to MicroVision, and the company has already shipped IRIS units within the first month since the acquisition.

Automotive revenue at scale is expected toward the end of the decade around 2029-2030 ramp-up, with the MOVIA S industrial launch on track for Q4 2025 and the 2026 revenue guidance weighted mostly toward the industrial segment.
Sangamo raised over $130 million in funding since the start of 2025 through nondilutive license fees, milestone payments, and equity financing.
The rolling submission of a BLA to the U.S. FDA for ST-920 in Fabry disease is in progress, with both the nonclinical and clinical modules already submitted.
The FDA reiterated in October 2025 that positive mean annualized eGFR slope at 52 weeks may serve as the primary basis of approval under an accelerated approval pathway for ST-920.
Sangamo anticipates completing submission of the Fabry BLA as early as summer 2026, subject to its ability to secure adequate additional funding.
Process validation lots for ST-920 manufacturing have been completed with acceptable results, method validation is complete, and the first commercial lot has been manufactured.
In April, Sangamo announced a third neurology capsid (STAC-BBB) license agreement with Eli Lilly for up to 5 central nervous system disease targets.
Most of the prior Fabry partnership counterparties from last year have dropped out, often due to regulatory uncertainty, and Sangamo is now in discussions with multiple new potential partners.
Six clinical sites have been activated in the Phase I/II STAND study evaluating ST-503 for chronic neuropathic pain due to small fiber neuropathy, with sites currently identifying patients.
ST-503 received Fast Track designation from the FDA in December for patients with intractable pain due to small fiber neuropathy.
The company acknowledged it has not yet solved its long-term cash runway, with securing a commercial partner for Fabry disease described as its number one focus.
Excelerate delivered Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $122 million (up ~9% sequentially) and net income of $50 million (up 28% sequentially), with a 99.8% asset reliability rate.

Full year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was revised to $480-$510 million, reflecting the delayed startup of the Iraq LNG import terminal, with committed growth capital now expected at $270-$300 million.

The Iraq integrated import terminal startup has been pushed from Q3 2026 into 2027 due to Middle East conflict-driven logistical constraints, with the 60-month contract beginning only once operations commence (~6 months after construction resumes).

Excelerate signed a 9-month time charter with Jordan's NEPCO to deploy the newbuild FSRU Acadia (delivered in early April) starting mid-2026, expected to generate roughly $20 million of adjusted EBITDA this year.

QatarEnergy issued a Force Majeure notice in March on the supply agreement, which Excelerate passed through back-to-back to Petrobangla in Bangladesh, with expected financial impact of approximately $1 million per month while the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

As of March 31, 2026, total debt including finance leases was $1.3 billion, cash was $540 million, net debt was $714 million, trailing net leverage was 1.5x, and the full $500 million revolver was available.

The Board approved a quarterly dividend of $0.08 per share ($0.32 annualized) payable June 4, 2026, and the company repurchased ~148,000 shares for just over $5 million at a weighted average price of $34.07 in Q1 under its $75 million buyback authorization.

The Express FSRU is expected to enter dry dock at the end of Q3 2026 and then redeploy to Pakistan in Q4 to substitute for the Exquisite, which will then enter its own dry dock; 2026 maintenance CapEx guidance is unchanged at $100-$110 million.

Management signed a letter of intent with Seatrium Shipyard in Singapore for the FSRU conversion, with associated costs not yet included in revised 2026 committed growth capital guidance, and the converted vessel is expected to support earnings growth in 2028.

Management reiterated that ~200 million tons of new LNG supply will come online by end of decade and views current conditions as supply disruption rather than demand destruction, framing Express redeployment in 2027 and the FSRU conversion in 2028 as the sequenced growth path.
Full year 2025 total revenue was $249.3 million, with subscription revenue representing 53% of total revenue, up from 45% in 2024.
Fourth quarter 2025 total revenue was $55.3 million, representing a 22.1% year-over-year decline.
Full year 2025 net loss and adjusted EBITDA losses were each reduced by approximately $100 million compared to the prior year.
Fourth quarter 2025 adjusted EBITDA loss was $10.3 million, a 55% improvement from the $22.8 million loss in Q4 2024.
The company ended 2025 with approximately $182 million in cash and marketable securities and no debt.
Full year 2026 revenue guidance is $195 million to $205 million, with adjusted EBITDA loss expected in the range of $24 million to $18 million.
First quarter 2026 revenue guidance is $48 million to $53 million, with an adjusted EBITDA loss in the range of $7 million to $5 million.
The company expects to achieve positive cash flow from operations in the fourth quarter of 2026.
In 2025, the company executed over 15 payer contract renewals representing the vast majority of existing payer subscription revenue, including a 3-year renewal with Elevance.
The company's current pipeline is the largest in its history, with participation in RFIs/RFPs across all 50 states, though none of the government pipeline revenue has been built into the 2026 plan.
Q3 2025 orders grew 4% year-over-year to 3,636 units, while average absorption pace declined 7% to 3.8 per month.
Home closing gross margin declined 570 basis points year-over-year to 19.1%, driven by increased incentives, inventory impairments, higher lot costs, and reduced fixed cost leverage.
Excluding $14.5 million in combined real estate inventory impairments and terminated land charges, adjusted diluted EPS was $1.55, representing a 42% decline from $2.67 in Q3 2024.
Community count reached a company-record 334 at quarter end, up 20% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, with management expecting double-digit year-over-year growth in 2026.
The company reduced lot acquisitions by approximately 5,800 lots or 70% year-over-year while maintaining near-term community count growth targets.
Cycle times improved to approximately 105 calendar days from 110 days in Q2, contributing to a 211% backlog conversion rate.

The Board approved an additional $500 million in share repurchase authorization, with $664 million now available under the program, and management indicated the current quarterly pace of $55 million is the floor for future buybacks.
Q4 2025 guidance includes home closings of 3,800-4,000 units, gross margin of 19-20%, and diluted EPS of $1.51-$1.70, with management expecting higher incentive usage typical of year-end.
Direct cost per square foot decreased 3% year-over-year, though management cautioned that potential tariffs and immigration policy changes could impact costs in 2026.

Management stated that stabilizing land acquisition and development costs are expected to benefit gross margins in late 2027 and into 2028, with the long-term gross margin target remaining at 22.5-23.5%.

Q1 2026 growth is skewed toward Q3 due to strong global stadium and U.S. amphitheater growth concentrated in summer months, with Q4 also shaping up to be very strong, implying AOI weighting more heavily to the back half versus prior years.
Concert cancellation rates are running slightly below the historical industry norm of 1%-2%, with roughly 100 cancellations expected out of ~15,000 shows on sale in 2026.
Amphitheater show count is tracking ahead of last year with ticket sales up over double digits, and early on-site premium sales data is positive days into the season.

Ticketing segment faces a mid-single-digit headwind this year from structural one-time steps taken to limit broker inventory on Ticketmaster's secondary platform, but management still expects Ticketmaster growth for the full year.
Secondary ticketing, previously a low double-digit percent of fee-bearing GTV, is expected to gradually decline into the single digits over the next several years as primary ticketing wins.
The company completed an initial venue securitization raise of just over EUR 600 million collateralized by venues, creating a PropCo-like financing vehicle to fund continued Venue Nation expansion.

CapEx has scaled from $400 million three years ago to $600 million, then $1 billion in 2025, and is expected to be equal or higher in 2026, with venue openings expected to accelerate into 2027 and 2028.
Maintenance CapEx on the concert side is only a couple of hundred million dollars, with Ticketmaster characterized as an extremely high cash flow conversion business.
Venue Nation fan count is expected to grow double digits in 2026 off the prior 65 million base, with growth split roughly evenly between existing venue performance and added venues.

Premium capacity is being scaled from historically 1%-5% up to as much as 25%-30% in new builds and retrofitted amphitheaters (Indianapolis, Dallas), with Hollywood Palladium's Vinyl Room already driving on-site spending over $100 per fan.
Q3 2025 revenue was $45.9 million, down 13.3% year-over-year and 3.5% sequentially, at about the midpoint of guidance range of $44-48 million.
Q3 gross profit margin was 18.6%, at the low end of guidance, down from 22% year-over-year and 20.4% sequentially due to ASP erosion particularly in China and lower fab utilization.
Communications segment revenue increased 34% sequentially and 95% year-over-year in Q3, showing significant strength.
Q4 2025 revenue guidance is $38.5-42.5 million with gross profit margin of 8-10%, including a 600 basis point negative impact from a $2.5 million channel inventory incentive program.
The company launched 30 new-generation products in the first 9 months of 2025 compared to only 2 in the same period of 2024, with at least 50 total expected in 2025 versus 4 in all of 2024.
New-generation products contributed 2% of total revenue in Q3 and are expected to reach approximately 10% in Q4 and throughout 2026.
Overall headcount is expected to be reduced by more than 20% by end of 2025 versus end of 2024, with non-factory employees reduced by nearly 40%.
CapEx for Gumi fab upgrade was cut by more than 50% from $65-70 million to $30-35 million through 2027 to conserve cash.
Cash balance ended Q3 at $108 million and is expected to decline to mid-$90 million by end of 2025.
Management expects Q1 2026 top line revenue to grow by double digits sequentially, though 2026 will remain a challenging gross margin period due to ongoing pricing pressure on legacy products.
Q3 2025 net sales of $47.3 million exceeded guidance of $41 million and represented 15.4% sequential growth from Q2 2025.
Gross margin expanded to 27.2% in Q3 2025 compared to 21.6% in Q3 2024, driven by higher proprietary brand penetration.
Adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.3 million, a $3.7 million improvement year-over-year and the company's strongest adjusted EBITDA performance in four years.
Proprietary brand sales reached 31.6% of cultivation and gardening revenue, up from 23.8% in the prior year period.
Total operating expenses decreased 31.5% year-over-year to $15.7 million, while store operating expenses declined 27.8% to $7.2 million.
The company ended Q3 2025 with $48.3 million in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities and no debt.
GAAP net loss narrowed to $2.4 million or negative $0.04 per share compared to a net loss of $11.4 million or negative $0.19 per share in Q3 2024.
Management expects Q4 2025 revenue of approximately $40 million, which would represent the first year-over-year quarterly revenue growth since 2021.
The company closed 5 stores during Q3, bringing the total to 24 locations, with 19 fewer retail locations since July 2024.
Management expects proprietary brands to reach approximately 40% of cultivation and gardening revenue in 2026 and anticipates positive revenue growth and positive adjusted EBITDA for the full year.
Q1 2026 revenue totaled $759.9 million, growing 27% as reported and 25.5% on a constant currency basis versus the prior year quarter.
Fully diluted non-GAAP EPS reached a Q1 record of $1.12, growing 64.7% over the prior year quarter, versus $0.68 in Q1 2025.
Globus raised full year 2026 non-GAAP fully diluted EPS guidance to $4.70–$4.80 (from $4.40–$4.50), while reaffirming revenue guidance of $3.18–$3.22 billion (implying 8.2%–9.6% growth).

U.S. Spine grew 9.6% as reported, marking the third consecutive quarter of ~10% growth and 58 weeks of consecutive growth, with management attributing the majority of growth to share gains against an estimated ~3% market.
Adjusted gross profit margin expanded to 69.2% versus 67.3% in the prior year quarter, with management reiterating a 69%–70% full year 2026 target and a long-term mid-70s goal.

Enabling Technologies revenue was $26.9 million, up 21.1%, but management is shifting the pipeline mix toward leases/rentals versus historical outright sales, which will reduce upfront revenue recognition.

Nevro contributed $82.7 million in Q1, declining 17.1% sequentially from Q4 2025, with management expecting it to potentially worsen before returning to historical run-rate revenue late in the second half of 2026.

Trauma revenue grew 30.4% year-over-year, driven by core trauma share gains, the ANTHEM Elbow plating system, and Precice Limb Lengthening now that manufacturing output has surpassed the former NuVasive facility's output.
International Spine grew 16.4% as reported and 9.8% on a constant currency basis, benefiting from not repeating prior-year supply chain disruptions, with long-term growth expectations of 12%–15%.

Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities rose to $799.3 million (from $629.1 million at year-end 2025) on $202.4 million of operating cash flow, with $390 million remaining under the $500 million share repurchase authorization.
Q3 2025 revenue was $10.1 million, representing a more than 580% increase year-over-year and nearly 60% sequential growth from Q2.
The company raised its full year 2025 revenue target to at least $36 million, implying Q4 revenue of more than $15 million.
Ondas established a 2026 revenue target of at least $110 million, which does not include any additional M&A beyond announced acquisitions.
Consolidated backlog grew to $23.3 million as of September 30, 2025, more than double from the start of the year, and exceeds $40 million when including closed or pending Q4 acquisitions.
Cash position was $433 million as of September 30, 2025, with pro forma cash of $840.4 million after the $407 million net proceeds from the October 7, 2025 equity offering.
The company raised approximately $855 million in equity during 2025 to support its growth plan.
Gross profit was $2.6 million in Q3 2025 with a 26% gross margin, compared to $0.05 million gross profit in Q3 2024.
The M&A pipeline includes over 20 companies with advanced activity on 7 potential targets, collectively representing more than $500 million in potential additional revenue.
Sentrycs has over 200 global deployments across more than 25 countries with gross margins in the upper 70% range and triple-digit compound annual growth rate in bookings.
Management expects operating businesses to reach EBITDA positive by the second half of 2026, with a target gross margin of 50%.
Eagle Materials achieved record quarterly revenue of $639 million, up 2% from the prior year.
Q2 fiscal 2026 EPS was $4.23, down 1% from the second quarter of fiscal 2025.
Cement sales volume increased 8% year-over-year while net cement sales prices declined 1%.
Wallboard sales volume decreased approximately 14% in Q2, with Wallboard sales prices down 2%.
The $430 million Laramie, Wyoming cement plant modernization is expected to reduce manufacturing costs by 25% and is on track for completion by end of calendar 2026.
The Duke, Oklahoma Wallboard plant upgrade is expected to lower per unit production costs by approximately 20%.
Aggregate sales volume increased 103% including acquisitions, with organic aggregate sales volume up 35%.
The company repurchased approximately 396,000 shares for $89 million in Q2, returning a total of $97 million to shareholders including dividends.
Total company capital spending for fiscal 2026 is expected to be in the range of $475 million to $500 million, with fiscal 2027 expected to be $400 million to $425 million.
Net debt-to-EBITDA leverage ratio was 1.6x with total committed liquidity of approximately $520 million at quarter end.
The company raised its 2025 earnings guidance to $6.48-$6.54 per diluted share, up from $6.34-$6.46, with the new midpoint representing an 18.4% increase over 2024 results.
Q3 adjusted diluted earnings per share was $1.64, an increase of 18% year-over-year.
Same-store and transitioning occupancy reached all-time highs of 83% and 84.4%, respectively, during the quarter.
Annual revenue guidance was increased to $5.05-$5.07 billion, up from $4.99-$5.02 billion.
The company added 22 new operations including 1,857 skilled nursing beds and 109 senior living units across 6 states during and since the quarter, bringing 2025 acquisitions to 45 operations.
Same-store skilled days increased 5.1% and transitioning skilled days increased 10.9% over the prior year quarter.
Managed care revenue increased 7.1% for same-store operations and 24.3% for transitioning operations year-over-year.
The company has over $1 billion in dry powder for future investments, including $443.7 million in cash and $593 million available under its credit line.
Lease adjusted net debt-to-EBITDA ratio stood at 1.86x after spending more than $240 million on strategic growth during the first nine months of 2025.
River Park Post Acute in Arizona increased occupancy from 76.3% to 97.1% year-over-year with EBIT up 376%, demonstrating the company's transitioning portfolio potential.
Net earnings rose to $14.6 million or $0.74 per diluted share compared to $4.7 million or $0.24 per share in the same period last year.

Q2 2026 revenue was $692 million, up 39% year-over-year, with GAAP EPS of $11.14 (up 69%) and non-GAAP EPS of $12.50 (up 60%).

The NBC broadcast deal will deliver a $10 million increase in adjusted EBITDA for 2026.
The company generated $166 million or $2.34 per share of free cash flow in Q3, with free cash flow per share up 13% from the prior year quarter.
Same-store Virginia HRM properties generated a combined 51% margin during the third quarter, which management described as best in class and sustainable.

Q1 2026 revenue was $55.9 million, down 6% year-over-year, at the upper end of guidance, with Life Sciences declining while Diversified and Provider segments (60%+ of revenue) returned to modest growth.

The company recorded a $197 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge as of March 31 due to the recent stock price decline, partially offset by a $6.6 million TRA remeasurement gain and $3.6 million deferred tax benefit.

Deferred revenue declined 12% year-over-year to $99 million, total RPO declined 18%, and current RPO declined 12% to $161 million, largely driven by a shift toward single-year versus multi-year deals (~$15M cRPO headwind).
Q2 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $55-56 million (down 8-9% YoY, worsening modestly as the data partnership benefit fully anniversaries) and adjusted EBITDA of $13.5-14.5 million (24-26% margin).
Full-year 2026 guidance was maintained at $220-226 million revenue (down 6-9%), with adjusted EBITDA raised by $1.5 million at the midpoint to $55-59 million (25-26% margin) and EPS of $0.16-$0.19.

Net dollar retention improved year-over-year on a trailing 12-month basis, and the company had its highest win-back quarter in over three years, including several 6-figure win-backs in Diversified and Med Tech.
Professional services revenue grew 25% year-over-year in Q1, with double-digit growth expected throughout 2026 driven by analytics engagements and digital activation ramp.

Integration time improved from over 100 days to approximately 45 days in Q1 (from 73 days in Q4), with 75% more integrations completed in the last six months versus the prior six months, and nearly 50 new integrations completed in Q1.

The first AI-enabled solutions are expected to launch later in Q2, with digital activation now having 30+ signed agencies (over half actively generating bookings, up from ~one-third last quarter) and audience click-through rates 63% higher than a leading competitor.
Adjusted net operating income was $206 million, up 7% year-over-year, while diluted adjusted operating EPS increased 11% to $6.33.
The company returned $163 million to stockholders in Q3 through $129 million in share repurchases and $34 million in dividends, totaling $479 million returned year-to-date.
Term Life policies issued were 79,379, down 15% year-over-year, with full year 2025 policies projected to decline around 10% compared to 2024's record-setting pace.
Investment and Savings Products (ISP) sales grew 28% year-over-year to a record $3.7 billion, with full year ISP sales expected to grow around 20% in 2025.
Client asset values ended the quarter at $127 billion, up 14% year-over-year, while net inflows were $363 million compared to $255 million in the prior year period.
Term Life segment revenues of $463 million rose 3% year-over-year, driven by a 5% increase in adjusted direct premiums, while pretax income declined 3% to $173 million.
ISP segment operating revenues increased 20% to $319 million, while pretax income rose 18% to $94 million.
The company completed its annual actuarial assumption review, resulting in a $23 million remeasurement gain primarily from mortality assumption changes reflecting favorable trends since the pandemic.
Primerica Life's estimated RBC ratio was 515%, and the holding company ended the quarter with $370 million in cash and invested assets.
Management expects Q4 Term Life operating margin of around 21% due to accelerated technology investments, with full year operating margin expected to be above 22%.
Sales increased 3% organically year-over-year, marking the company's first quarter of organic growth in 2 years after 8 quarters of broad market weakness.
Adjusted EPS increased to $0.34 compared to $0.29 in the prior year quarter, while adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 15.3% from 14.3%.
The company raised its FY26 sales outlook to $2.1 billion to $2.17 billion and adjusted EPS outlook to $1.35 to $1.65.
The company realized $8 million in restructuring savings this quarter and remains on track for $35 million in total restructuring savings for the year.
Aerospace and Defense sales grew 20% on a constant currency basis, driven by improved build rates and easing supply chain pressures.
Free operating cash flow decreased to negative $5 million from positive $21 million in the prior year, primarily due to higher inventory investment from rising tungsten prices.
The company returned $25 million to shareholders through $10 million in share repurchases (475,000 shares) and $15 million in dividends.
Net price and tariff surcharge combined is expected to contribute approximately 7% to FY26 sales, up from the prior outlook of approximately 4%.
The Power Generation market represents a $250 million total addressable market that is projected to grow at a 10% CAGR over the next few years.
The company maintained combined cash and revolver availability of approximately $800 million with no near-term debt refunding requirements.
Q4 FY26 revenue was $448.5 million, above the midpoint of guidance, down 23% sequentially due to lower smartphone unit volumes but up 6% year-over-year.
Full fiscal year 2026 delivered record revenue of $2 billion, up 5% year-over-year, with record non-GAAP EPS of $9.26 versus $7.54 in FY25.

Q1 FY27 revenue guidance is $430–$490 million (up 3% sequentially and 13% year-over-year at midpoint) with gross margin guided to 51%–53% and OpEx of $132–$138 million, up sequentially largely due to increased R&D.
Management expects a smaller-than-typical delta between the June and September quarters, as a greater proportion of content is ramping earlier than in the past.
Non-GAAP gross margin was 53% in Q4 and 52.8% for FY26, with the year-over-year Q4 decline driven primarily by higher freight expenses.

Cirrus ended FY26 with approximately $1.2 billion in cash and investments (up $319 million YoY), no debt, and $274.1 million remaining on its share repurchase authorization after returning $280 million to shareholders via buybacks during FY26.
Inventory rose to $240.9 million (104 days) from $189.5 million in Q3, while Q4 cash flow from operations was $151.4 million and FY26 free cash flow margin was 32%.

PC revenue grew from low tens of millions in FY25 to the $40 million range in FY26, with SDCA tripling to nearly 60% of PC revenue and expected to reach ~80% in FY27, while mainstream devices are expected to exceed half of PC revenue in FY27.

Cirrus is in the design phase of its first smart power IC for 3D sensing/Face ID, with management indicating roughly a couple of years before introduction, marking a new application space with its largest customer.

Cirrus joined its largest customer's American manufacturing program and is working with GlobalFoundries to manufacture high-voltage products (amplifiers, haptics drivers, power conversion) at the Malta, New York facility on next-generation processes.
Avery Dennison delivered Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.37, up 2% year-over-year and above the midpoint of expectations.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA margin was 16.5%, up 10 basis points compared to prior year.
The company generated adjusted free cash flow of nearly $270 million in Q3 with a net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio of 2.2.

Year-to-date, the company repurchased approximately $454 million in stock and grew its dividend by 7%, returning roughly $670 million to shareholders through repurchases and dividends in the first 9 months.

Avery Dennison announced a major partnership with Walmart to deploy RFID solutions in fresh grocery categories (bakery, meat, and deli), which management estimates could drive high single-digit to low double-digit growth on total 2025 enterprise Intelligent Labels revenue over a 2-year rollout period.
High-value categories now represent 45% of total business year-to-date, an increase compared to prior year.
Enterprise-wide Intelligent Labels sales grew approximately 3% compared to prior year, with food, logistics, and industrial categories combined up mid-single digits.
Materials Group adjusted EBITDA margin was 17.5% in Q3, up 50 basis points year-over-year, driven by productivity and modest volume mix growth.
Q4 guidance calls for reported sales growth of 5% to 7% and adjusted EPS of $2.35 to $2.45, with organic growth expected at 0% to 2%.
The company closed the $390 million Taylor Adhesives acquisition and issued a EUR 500 million note to fund it, with full-year interest expense now expected to be approximately $135 million.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 61.6% year-over-year in Q3 2025 to $38.2 million, with EBITDA margin as a percentage of care margin expanding 720 basis points to reach 30.5%.

Privia agreed to acquire Evolent Health's ACO business for $100 million in cash plus an earn-out of up to $13 million, adding over 120,000 value-based care attributed lives across existing and new states.
Practice collections increased 27.1% year-over-year in Q3 2025 to reach $940.4 million.
Across Privia's 9 ACOs in MSSP for 2024, the company managed over $2.5 billion in medical spend with an aggregate savings rate of 9.4%, up from 8.2% in 2023.
Total shared savings in MSSP of $234.1 million increased 32.6% year-over-year, with Privia's gross shared savings (after CMS' share) reaching $160.1 million, a 36% increase over 2023.
Pro forma cash at the end of Q3 2025 was $409.9 million with no debt, assuming deployment of $100 million for the ACO acquisition and net cash received from CMS for 2024 MSSP performance.
Total value-based attributed lives increased close to 13% year-over-year to over 1.4 million patients, with the Evolent acquisition expected to expand total attributed lives to more than 1.5 million.
For the first 9 months of 2025, adjusted EBITDA grew 43.5% to reach $94.1 million, and year-to-date pro forma free cash flow (excluding business development transactions) was $104.4 million.
Updated 2025 guidance projects adjusted EBITDA growth of 32% at the midpoint, with more than 80% of full year adjusted EBITDA expected to convert to free cash flow.

The Mid-Atlantic ACO, caring for about 60,000 patients, delivered an 11% savings rate, which for the fifth consecutive year was the highest savings rate of all ACOs with greater than 40,000 attributed lives.
ResMed delivered Q2 FY2026 revenue of $1.42 billion, representing 11% headline growth and 9% growth on a constant currency basis.
GAAP earnings per share grew 16% year-over-year, while operating profit increased 19%.
Gross margin expanded 310 basis points year-over-year to 62.3%, with the company now guiding to 62%-63% gross margin for fiscal year 2026.
Global masks and other sales increased 14% on a constant currency basis, with U.S., Canada and Latin America masks and other sales up 16%.
Claims data tracking 1.95 million patients shows GLP-1 users are 10%-11% more likely to start CPAP therapy and 6% more likely to have a resupply event at 3 years compared to non-GLP-1 patients.
ResMed returned $263 million to shareholders in Q2, including $175 million in share repurchases, and plans to repurchase more than $600 million in shares for fiscal year 2026.

CME programs for primary care physicians have been completed nearly 60,000 times, a 50% increase from Q1 FY2026, with 77% of providers intending to change their clinical practices related to sleep apnea.
CPAP, APAP and bilevel products were excluded from CMS's upcoming competitive bidding program for the first time in 15 years.
The company ended Q2 with $1.4 billion in cash, $753 million in net cash, and $1.5 billion available under its revolver facility.
Europe, Asia and Rest of World masks, accessories and other revenue reaccelerated to 8% growth on a constant currency basis, in line with management's prior quarter guidance.
Full year 2025 revenues were $15.1 billion, down approximately 1% organically, with adjusted earnings per share growing 7% to $4.67.
Fourth quarter 2025 organic revenue declined 3%, which was below the company's expectations, with a 7% volume decline partially offset by a 4% price increase.
The adjusted gross margin expanded 70 basis points to 30.7% for full year 2025, with Q4 adjusted gross margin reaching 33.3%, up 210 basis points year-over-year.
The company completed its global cost reduction program, capturing $2.1 billion of run rate pretax cost savings since mid-2022, including approximately $120 million of incremental savings in Q4.

Stanley Black & Decker announced the sale of its Aerospace fasteners business (CAM) for $1.8 billion in cash, with expected net proceeds of $1.525 billion to $1.6 billion to be used for debt reduction.
For 2026, the company expects adjusted earnings per share of $4.90 to $5.70, representing 13% growth at the midpoint, with free cash flow generation of $700 million to $900 million.
Tools & Outdoor Q4 organic revenue declined 4%, with a 9% volume decline largely due to softness in opening price point products and promotional sensitivity in North American retail channels.
The Aerospace business delivered 35% organic growth in Q4, while the broader Engineered Fastening segment achieved 8% organic growth for the quarter.
The company expects Q1 2026 adjusted EPS of approximately $0.55 to $0.60, with adjusted gross margin roughly flat year-over-year due to peak tariff expense rolling off the balance sheet.
Management expects to reduce China imports for U.S. consumption from approximately 20% to less than 5% by the end of 2026, running ahead of its original tariff mitigation plan.

Park-Ohio expects 2026 consolidated revenues of $1.675 billion to $1.71 billion, representing 5% to 7% growth over 2025, with adjusted EPS of $2.90 to $3.20 per diluted share, an increase of 7% to 19% year-over-year.
The company generated $49 million in operating cash flow and $36 million in free cash flow in Q4 2025, using proceeds to reduce long-term debt by $40 million during the quarter.

Industrial Equipment achieved record annual bookings of $217 million, including a record $47 million induction heating order from a leading steel producer, resulting in backlogs of $180 million at December 31, up 24% year-over-year.
Supply Technologies' AI data center-related revenues grew from very little two years ago to approaching $150 million annually, with continued growth expected in 2026 and beyond.
Assembly Components won over $40 million of incremental annual new business during 2025, with launches in the second half of 2026 continuing through 2027.
Full year 2025 adjusted EPS was $2.70 compared to $3.59 in 2024, while Q4 2025 adjusted EPS was $0.65 versus $0.67 in Q4 2024, with the decrease driven primarily by higher interest expense.

The company invested over $12 million in information technology during 2025, including new ERP systems in Supply Technologies and the Industrial Equipment Group, and broke ground on a new state-of-the-art North American distribution center expected to be operational in 2026.
Supply Technologies Q4 operating income increased 31% to $21 million with operating margin expanding 240 basis points to 11.1% of sales, driven by higher sales and cost control measures.
The company's 2025 effective tax rate was 12% due to R&D tax credits, but is expected to normalize to 18% to 20% in 2026.

Approximately 75% of the guided 2026 revenue growth is expected to come from production volume increases, with automotive exposure reduced from over one-third of revenue historically to slightly over 20% currently.
Q4 adjusted EBITDA was $27.8 million, representing a 35% margin, and revenue and adjusted EBITDA both exceeded guidance.
Excluding political revenues and the legacy DSP impact, 83% of PubMatic's Q4 business grew 18% year-over-year.
Full-year CTV grew over 50% year-over-year excluding political, with a four-year compound annual growth rate of over 50%, and PubMatic now partners with 28 of the top 30 global streamers.

Emerging revenues (including Activate, commerce media, and AI solutions) nearly doubled over 2024, grew over 75% year-over-year in Q4, and now represent roughly 12% of total Q4 revenues, up from less than 1% three years ago.
Free cash flow was $46 million for the full year, a 32% increase over 2024, and the company ended Q4 with $145.5 million in cash and zero debt.

Q1 2026 revenue guidance is $58 million to $60 million with adjusted EBITDA of negative $0.5 million to positive $1 million, and management expects to return to double-digit revenue growth in the second half of 2026.

Since inception of the share repurchase program in February 2023 through Q4, the company has bought back 12.4 million shares for $181.1 million, with $93.9 million remaining authorized through end of 2026.

Over 250 agentic deals have already been run across the platform, and nearly 100 brands, agencies, and streamers have applied to join the Agentic AI Accelerator Program, making it the fastest early-stage adoption of any product PubMatic has launched.
Ad spend from mid-market DSP partners grew 30% year-over-year in Q4, accelerating from 25% in Q3, supported by the addition of 50 new DSP partnerships in 2025.
PubMatic processed 337 trillion impressions in 2025, up 28% year-over-year, while keeping cost of revenues relatively flat, with unit costs declining 20% year-over-year on a trailing 12-month basis.
EQT generated $2.5 billion of free cash flow attributable to EQT in 2025 with NYMEX natural gas prices averaging approximately $3.40 per MMBtu for the year.

At recent strip pricing, EQT expects 2026 adjusted EBITDA attributable to EQT of approximately $6.5 billion and 2026 free cash flow attributable to EQT of $3.5 billion, including approximately $600 million in growth investments.

EQT sold approximately 98% of its February production at first-of-month pricing, which settled at $7.22 per MMBtu for M2 and $7.46 per MMBtu for Henry Hub, with potential free cash flow in February alone approaching $1 billion.

EQT's average 2025 well cost per lateral foot came in 13% lower year-over-year and 6% below internal forecast, while per unit LOE was nearly 15% below expectations and approximately 50% lower than the peer average.
EQT expects to exit Q1 2026 with less than $6 billion of net debt, down from just under $7.7 billion at year-end 2025, rapidly approaching its $5 billion long-term target.
Cumulative free cash flow attributable to EQT over the next 5 years is projected to total more than $16 billion.

EQT is allocating the first $600 million of post-dividend free cash flow to high-return growth projects in 2026, including compression, water infrastructure, the 400 million cubic feet per day Clarington Connector Pipeline, and strategic leasing.

EQT exercised its option to purchase additional interest in MVP Mainline and MVP Boost, funding approximately $115 million, increasing ownership to approximately 53%, at roughly 9x adjusted EBITDA and delivering an estimated 12% IRR.

EQT's marketing optimization efforts resulted in more than $200 million of free cash flow uplift in 2025 relative to guidance, and January-February 2026 performance already exceeds consensus Q1 free cash flow expectations by more than 30%.

EQT is nearly 40% hedged in Q1 2026 with an average floor of $4.30/MMBtu and ceiling of $6.30, approximately 20% hedged in Q2-Q3 with $3.50 floors and nearly $5 ceilings, and roughly 20% hedged in Q4 with $3.75 floors and $5.15 ceilings.
Q3 2025 revenue was $118.8 million, up slightly year-over-year, marking an inflection point after consecutive periods of year-over-year declines.
Gross margin improved nearly 700 basis points sequentially to 42.8% in Q3, up from 36% in Q2, despite tariff-related headwinds of approximately $2 million.
The Mattress Firm expansion represents approximately $20 million in incremental revenue in 2025 and approximately $70 million anticipated in 2026.
Purple products are now represented in approximately 9,200 Mattress Firm slots and the company is on pace to reach 12,000 slots by March 2026.

Rejuvenate 2.0 has sold more than twice the number of units, doubling net revenue compared to Rejuvenate 1.0 in showrooms, with over 3,000 units sold through direct channels at an average sales price of approximately $5,800.
Showroom comparable sales grew 12% in Q3 with record mattress order values of approximately $4,500, and 76% of showrooms are now profitable year-to-date versus 56% last year.
Adjusted EBITDA was positive $200,000 in Q3, an improvement from a loss of $6.4 million in the prior year period.

The company's restructuring program is expected to deliver $25 million to $30 million in annual savings, with the breakeven point improved from $55-60+ million per month to approximately $40 million per month.
E-commerce revenue was down 9.8% in Q3, while wholesale net revenue of $51.5 million was up 7.9% year-over-year.
The company reiterated full year 2025 guidance of revenue between $465 million and $485 million and adjusted EBITDA between breakeven and $10 million positive.
Q1 FY26 sales of $1.1 billion were 21% higher than the prior year's first quarter, with record quarterly sales in all four segments.
12-month backlog increased by 30% year-over-year, setting a new record.
Adjusted earnings per share of $2.63 increased 37% compared to Q1 FY25.
Space and Defense segment sales reached a record $324 million, up 31% year-over-year, driven by strong missile control and satellite component demand.
Adjusted operating margin was 13.0%, up 90 basis points year-over-year, or up 220 basis points excluding tariff pressure.

The company secured over $1 billion in Commercial Aircraft orders, an additional PAC-3 missile order exceeding $100 million, and a new space vehicle contract exceeding $100 million for Meteor satellites.
FY26 adjusted EPS guidance was raised by $0.20 to $10.20 plus or minus $0.20, reflecting stronger-than-expected sales growth.
Tariffs created approximately 300 basis points of margin pressure on the Commercial Aircraft segment in Q1.
The missiles business exceeded $200 million in FY25 with approximately 20% annual growth and is expected to exceed $250 million in FY26.

Data center cooling pump sales are expected to double from approximately $25 million in FY25 to about $50 million in FY26, with production rates increasing from 200 pumps per week to over 500 pumps per week.
Total revenue of $192 million increased 11% year-over-year normalized for third quarter 2024 cyclical political campaign revenue.
Cloud communications revenue reached $142 million, an 8% year-over-year increase on a normalized basis.
Adjusted EBITDA was $24 million, exceeding expectations and guidance ranges.
Enterprise voice revenue increased 22% year-over-year, reflecting strong adoption among existing customers and new customer ramp.
Global voice plans revenue grew 7% year-over-year, more than doubling the growth rate from last year.
Trailing 12-month free cash flow grew 35% year-over-year to underscore durability of cash generation.
Net retention rate was 107% when excluding the benefit from political campaign revenue in 2024.
Average annual revenue per customer set a record at $231,000, growing 46% over the last 3 years.
The company raised full year adjusted EBITDA outlook for the third time this year to $91 million at the midpoint, expected to represent about $1.30 non-GAAP earnings per share.
The company expects to end 2025 with an annualized MRR exit rate on software greater than $10 million.
Full year 2025 revenues of $12.5 billion grew 8.2% year-over-year, with EPS of $15.39 compared to $13.96 in 2024.
2025 awards totaled $16.9 billion, and the company is raising its medium-term shipbuilding revenue growth guidance from approximately 4% to approximately 6%.
2025 free cash flow was $800 million, exceeding the guidance range, with combined 2025-2026 free cash flow now expected at $1.35 billion versus the prior $1.2 billion two-year target.
Shipbuilding throughput increased 14% year-over-year in 2025, and the company has established a 2026 target to increase throughput by another 15%.

2026 guidance calls for shipbuilding revenues of $9.7 billion to $9.9 billion at 5.5% to 6.5% margins, Mission Technologies revenues of $3.0 billion to $3.2 billion at approximately 5% margins, and free cash flow of $500 million to $600 million.
The company hired over 6,600 shipbuilders in 2025 with a 15% to 18% improvement in attrition across both shipyards, and expects to hire at least as many in 2026.
Outsourcing doubled year-over-year in 2025 with over 23 vendors established, and the company plans to increase outsourcing by another 30% in 2026.
The Virginia-class Block VI and Columbia Build II submarine contracts are expected to be finalized in the first half of 2026, with guidance predicated on achieving these agreements.
2026 capital expenditures are expected to be approximately 4% to 5% of sales ($500 million to $600 million), a significant increase from the 3.2% of sales ($396 million) spent in 2025.
The medium-term 6% shipbuilding growth target does not yet account for the recently announced frigate or Trump-class battleship programs, which represent additional upside to revenue forecasts.

Q4 2025 revenues rose to $75.4 million from $73 million in Q4 2024, representing 5.6% growth on an apples-to-apples basis after excluding $1.5 million of revenue from the divested Stockman's property.

Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $10.7 million, representing approximately a 23% increase over Q4 2024 after backing out $1.7 million of one-time benefits (a $1.2 million recovery settlement and $0.5 million accrual reversal) from the prior year period.

American Place temporary casino revenues increased 11% to $32 million in Q4 2025 with adjusted property EBITDA rising 29% to $8.7 million; full-year revenues and adjusted property EBITDA reached $124 million and $34.3 million, increases of 13% and 17% respectively.

Management believes the temporary American Place facility can eventually achieve approximately $50 million of run-rate EBITDA, and the permanent facility, which will be about twice the size, should earn approximately $100 million.

The company has received several financing proposals for the permanent American Place facility at rates described as acceptable (between 5% and 15%), including proposals that fully fund construction without any equity issuance, and expects to finalize details in the coming weeks.

A bill was recently introduced in the Illinois legislature to extend the temporary casino operating permit by 18 months beyond its current August 2027 expiration, with expected passage in April or May 2026.

Chamonix's second-half 2025 adjusted property EBITDA improved by $4.2 million compared to second-half 2024, with revenues increasing by $1.2 million (about 5%) in that same period under the new management team.

In the first two months of 2026, Chamonix's top database segment saw unique guest counts increase by almost 20% and total visits rise 36%, while the next segment saw unique guests up 12% and total visits up 24%.
The company had approximately $51 million of liquidity at quarter-end, including the undrawn portion of its revolver, which was just amended to extend its maturity to August 15, 2027.
The American Place customer database has grown to approximately 121,000–125,000 names and continues to add new names at a pace similar to 3, 6, and 9 months ago with no signs of slowing down.
Q3 net sales reached a record $908 million, up 8.2% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA of $133 million (14.6% margin) also setting a quarterly record as a public company.
Adjusted earnings per share increased to $1.59 from $1.17 in the prior year quarter, a $0.42 improvement.
The company acquired SEM in August for $47 million total, comprised of $15 million in cash and $32 million to extinguish assumed debt.

SEM is expected to contribute approximately $50 million in annual sales and $10 million in adjusted operating income, though first-year results may face headwinds from the challenged commercial vehicle market.

The company returned $41 million to shareholders in Q3 through $11 million in dividends and $30 million in share repurchases, and has repurchased approximately 20% of outstanding shares since the July 2023 spin-off.
Adjusted free cash flow was $104 million in Q3, a significant increase from $60 million in the same period of the prior year.
The company raised its 2025 guidance midpoints, with sales now at $3.42 billion (up $40 million), adjusted EBITDA at $473 million, and adjusted free cash flow at $190 million (up $10 million).
Net leverage remains at 1.4x EBITDA with total liquidity of approximately $900 million and cash of $349 million.
The company announced a restructuring program with approximately $35 million in costs expected to yield $25 million in annual savings with less than 2-year payback once fully implemented.
The Fuel Systems segment adjusted operating income increased 33% with margin expanding 190 basis points year-over-year, driven by R&D savings and overhead cost control measures.
Third quarter revenue totaled $399 million, with year-over-year sales decline driven by lower end market demand in certain North American industrial markets.
Adjusted EPS was $0.65 per diluted share in Q3 2025, compared to $0.66 in Q1 and $0.75 in Q2 of this year.
The company generated EBITDA of $34.2 million in the quarter, representing an 8.6% EBITDA margin, with trailing 12-month EBITDA totaling $140 million.
Fourth quarter free cash flow is expected to range between $45 million to $55 million, with full year free cash flow estimated between $10 million to $20 million.
Capital equipment backlog totaled $185 million as of September 30, an increase of 28% compared to year-end, with the company expecting record annual bookings exceeding $200 million.

The company refinanced both its senior notes and revolving credit facility, extending maturity dates by 5 years, incurring $2 million in bond-related expenses that reduced GAAP earnings by $0.11 per share.
A $47 million order from a major steel producer for induction slab heating equipment will have 3 of 5 pieces of equipment recognized in 2026 and the remaining 2 in 2027.
Full year 2025 guidance includes net sales of $1.600 billion to $1.620 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $2.70 to $2.90 per diluted share.
The Assembly Components segment is currently launching over $50 million of incremental business across all product lines throughout 2026.
The company expects $35 million to $45 million of debt reduction in Q4 from free cash flow generation.

BARK guided FY2027 revenue of $325–340 million (down from $394.8M in FY26) and adjusted EBITDA of $7–10 million, a meaningful step-up from FY26's $0.2M, with Q1 FY27 revenue guided to $77–79M and EBITDA of $0–1M.
The Board authorized a $40 million share repurchase program to be funded by ongoing free cash flow, the first such program signaling confidence at current stock levels.

Full-year FY26 revenue declined to $394.8M from $484.2M, with Q4 revenue of $86.6M versus $115.4M prior year, reflecting a deliberate $24M+ year-over-year cut in marketing spend (FY26 marketing was $59.2M).
Management is sunsetting the Kibble and toppers product lines due to inadequate returns, reallocating capital to higher-return categories to simplify the business and improve profitability.

D2C revenue is expected to decline year-over-year in 1H FY27 before stabilizing in 2H and returning to growth, as the company enters FY27 with a smaller but higher-quality subscriber base showing improved retention and AOV (D2C gross margin rose 200+ bps to 68%).
Commerce and BARK Air are expected to collectively exceed $100M in FY27 revenue, with Commerce alone projected to grow to roughly 25% of total revenue versus 18% in FY26.
BARK Air revenue more than doubled to over $12.4M in FY26 with 90% utilization, but management is prioritizing unit economics over growth and does not expect significant revenue growth in FY27.
Q4 Commerce revenue fell 18.3% year-over-year to $12.5M due to timing of retail shipments, though full-year Commerce grew modestly to $59.9M (Matt cited $70M including a different segmentation).

The company ended FY26 debt-free with $19M cash and $75.5M inventory (down ~$13M YoY), and expects an additional $12.1M in IEEPA tariff refunds ($7.1M tied to FY26 COGS, $5M to FY27) to be recognized once eligible.
BARK diversified its toy supply chain away from near-total China reliance into multiple Southeast Asian countries and South America, enabling rapid failover if new China tariffs emerge.
IFF's net debt to credit adjusted EBITDA improved from 3.8x at the end of 2024 to 2.6x at the end of 2025, with gross debt decreasing by nearly $3 billion to approximately $6 billion.

Full year 2026 guidance calls for sales of $10.5 billion to $10.8 billion (1% to 4% comparable currency-neutral growth) and EBITDA of $2.05 billion to $2.15 billion (3% to 8% comparable currency-neutral growth).
Full year 2025 free cash flow was $256 million, including approximately $300 million of Reg G-related charges primarily driven by divestiture activities and a $166 million working capital outflow.
IFF formally launched the sale process for its Food Ingredients business approximately two weeks prior to the call, with strong interest from both strategic buyers and financial sponsors.

Health & Biosciences delivered Q4 EBITDA of $155 million, a 20% year-over-year increase, while the health sub-segment remained down low single digits and is expected to return to growth in the second half of 2026.

The company invested approximately $100 million in 2025 into innovation capabilities in high-growth, high-margin categories, with benefits expected to materialize in the second half of 2026 and more fully in 2027.
Incremental margins on volume growth are approximately 30% to 35% depending on the business segment, and 2026 growth is expected to be primarily volume-driven with pricing slightly down.

The Taste segment delivered Q4 EBITDA of $94 million, a 17% increase year-over-year, driven by high single-digit sales growth in North America from new wins, favorable net pricing, and cost discipline.

IFF returned $409 million to shareholders through dividends and $38 million through share repurchases in 2025, with a minimum annual share buyback target of $80 million to $100 million to offset dilution.

Q1 2026 is expected to show muted sales and only modest EBITDA growth versus a like-for-like Q1 2025 base of approximately $505 million (adjusted for divestitures), with year-over-year growth expected to progressively improve each quarter.
Q4 2025 revenue was approximately $2.55 billion with constant currency growth of 3.1%, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Full year fiscal 2025 delivered constant currency revenue growth of 2.1%, which was 60 basis points above the high end of guidance provided a year ago.
Record adjusted free cash flow of $626 million for fiscal 2025 represented a 32% increase (over $150 million) compared to the prior year.

The company returned $258 million to shareholders in fiscal 2025, including $169 million in share repurchases (approximately 3.6 million shares at an average price of $47) and $89 million in dividends.
A $1.52 billion noncash goodwill impairment charge was recorded in Q4, reflecting the trading range of the stock during the quarter.
The iX suite AI platform exited fiscal 2025 with over $60 million in annualized AI revenue and reached breakeven profitability.
Fiscal 2026 guidance includes reported revenue of $10.035 billion to $10.180 billion, implying constant currency growth of 1.5% to 3%.
Net debt was reduced by approximately $184 million during fiscal 2025 to $4.311 billion at year-end.
Banking, financial services and insurance clients grew 11% on a constant currency basis in Q4, the strongest performing vertical.
The company reduced expenditures on non-billable resources and infrastructure by close to $100 million on a run rate basis exiting Q1 2026.

Q1 2026 revenue was $336.6 million, up 2% year-over-year, but would have grown low double digits absent IRA-mandated price declines, which reduced pricing on Guardian's IRA-impacted branded drug mix by approximately 60%.

Adjusted EBITDA grew 27% year-over-year to $29.8 million (8.8% margin), or 14% growth and 8% margin excluding a $3 million discrete benefit from favorable payer dynamics and a manufacturer inventory credit tied to the IRA.
Gross profit rose 19% year-over-year to $76 million (22.7% margin), with the IRA representing an approximate $10 million headwind that management offset through proactive payor renegotiations.

Full-year 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $123–$127 million from $120–$124 million to reflect the $3 million discrete benefit, while revenue guidance was maintained at $1.40–$1.42 billion.
Total residents grew 10% year-over-year to approximately 207,000 (with assisted living ~70% of mix), and script volumes also increased 10% year-over-year.

SG&A included a $3.2 million legal expense (added back to adjusted EBITDA) related to payor reimbursement disputes, and a post-quarter settlement will generate an $8.5 million cash payment recognized as Q2 other income (excluded from adjusted EBITDA).
Cash ended the quarter at $65 million (flat with year-end) after absorbing a one-time IRA-related working capital impact, which accounted for roughly half of the working capital used in the quarter.

Acquisitions completed over the past two years dampened consolidated EBITDA margins by approximately 80 basis points, with management expecting a similar drag to persist through 2026 and 2027 as new deals are added.

Guardian completed a nondilutive secondary offering of 6.9 million Class A shares (including full overallotment) priced at $31 per share, and filed a new shelf registration with no current plans to utilize it.

Management flagged potential headwinds including elevated fuel costs (up to a few million dollars annually) and modestly higher labor costs from regional infrastructure investments, while noting Guardian holds only ~13–14% market share with substantial M&A pipeline runway.
Q3 2025 revenues were $202.7 million, with non-GAAP gross margins of 41%, up 250 basis points from 38.5% in Q2 2025.
Q3 non-GAAP EPS was $0.33, which was $0.04 above the high end of the outlook range of $0.21 to $0.29.
Q4 2025 revenue guidance is $210 million plus or minus $5 million, with non-GAAP gross margin expected at 42% plus or minus 150 basis points.
HBM revenue was approximately $40 million in Q3, close to the previous high, with most sequential DRAM growth driven by HBM.
The company continues to experience a 150 to 200 basis point negative impact on gross margins from tariffs.
Cash expenditures for the Farmers Branch, Texas manufacturing facility are expected to be between $140 million and $170 million over 2026.
Free cash flow was $19.7 million in Q3 compared to negative $47.1 million in Q2, with total cash and investments reaching $266 million at quarter end.
A recently completed headcount reduction is expected to provide approximately $1 million in cost savings in Q4 and about $1.5 million on an ongoing basis thereafter.
The company's largest CPU customer was not a 10% customer in Q3, indicating a significant revenue decline from that customer.
The company expects initial Farmers Branch capacity to come online late in 2026 with the majority of capacity coming online in 2027.

The FCC formally sent a draft Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) focused on PNT technology and solutions to the White House OMB earlier in March 2026, which the company describes as a critical step in the regulatory process.
NextNav finished Q4 2025 with approximately $152 million in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments.
A significant number of warrants expiring in 2026 have the potential to deliver over $200 million in additional capital depending on stock price performance.
In Q4 2025, NextNav recognized approximately $48 million in noncash losses associated with the change in fair value of derivative and warrant liabilities.
The net loss for Q4 2025 was roughly $68 million, driven primarily by noncash derivative and warrant liability losses.
NextNav has begun operating what it describes as the world's first 5G-powered PNT network under an FCC experimental license in a defined geographic location, independent of the FCC's NPRM process.
NextNav announced an expanded partnership with Japan's MetCom, which has licensed NextNav's technology to power new terrestrial timing services in major Japanese metropolitan areas.
The company's proposed solution does not require taxpayer funding and management believes it can be made available during the current administration.
NextNav CEO Mariam Sorond joined the CTIA Board of Directors, positioning the company alongside major telecommunications industry leaders.

Lisa Hook was appointed as the Board's new Lead Independent Director, bringing experience as former CEO of publicly traded Neustar and expertise at the intersection of technology, telecommunications, and national security.
Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $1.16 billion, exceeding guidance, with adjusted EPS of $0.58 up 13% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA margin expanding 140 bps to 17.6%.

IET delivered record bookings of $4.9 billion (third consecutive quarter above $4 billion) with a 1.5x book-to-bill, driving record RPO of $33.1 billion and IET EBITDA growth of 35% YoY to $678 million at a 20.2% margin (+310 bps).

Power Systems generated $1.4 billion in Q1 orders (~30% of total IET orders), including a 1 GW data center award, 25 BRUSH generators for Boom Supersonic (1.21 GW), and management estimates the behind-the-meter market reaching $60 billion by 2030.
LNG equipment orders totaled $1.2 billion in Q1, highlighted by a QatarEnergy award for 2 mega trains on North Field West (16 MTPA) including 6 Frame 9 turbines and 12 centrifugal compressors.
Management raised confidence that the Horizon 2 IET order target will exceed $40 billion by 2028, supported by structural energy security demand.

Baker Hughes expects approximately $3 billion in gross divestiture proceeds in 2026 from Waygate Technologies, the HMH IPO, PSI sale to Crane, and the SPC/Cactus JV, exceeding its $1 billion incremental divestment target ahead of schedule.

The Middle East conflict has taken ~10% of global oil volumes and 20% of worldwide LNG capacity offline, leading the company to revise its 2026 global upstream spending outlook to modestly below prior low-single-digit decline expectations.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for company revenue of $6.5 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $1.13 billion, with IET EBITDA of $670 million and OFSE EBITDA of $540 million on revenue of $3.2 billion, assuming Middle East revenue declines more than 20% sequentially.

Full-year 2026 guidance is maintained but expected to land slightly below the midpoint, with OFSE EBITDA likely at the low end of its $2.325 billion range and IET EBITDA at least the $2.7 billion midpoint.

Q1 free cash flow was $210 million, the balance sheet strengthened with net debt/EBITDA at 0.3x and a $14.8 billion cash position following a $6.5 billion U.S. bond and €3 billion inaugural European bond issuance to fund the Chart acquisition (expected to close in Q2 with $325 million targeted cost synergies).
Full year 2025 U.S. cabozantinib franchise net product revenues grew 17% year-over-year to approximately $2.12 billion.
Global cabozantinib franchise net product revenues generated by Exelixis and its partners were approximately $2.89 billion for full year 2025 and $754 million in Q4 2025.
Fourth quarter 2025 U.S. cabo franchise net product revenues were $547 million, representing 6% year-over-year growth.
CABOMETYX U.S. net product revenues exceeded $100 million for the neuroendocrine tumor indication in 2025, its first year on the market for that indication.
Gross to net for the cabozantinib franchise in Q4 2025 was 28.5%, lower than Q3 2025, and full year 2026 gross to net is estimated to be between 31% and 32%.

Cash and marketable securities as of December 31, 2025, were approximately $1.66 billion.
The FDA accepted the NDA submission for zanzalintinib plus atezolizumab in third-line plus CRC with a PDUFA target action date of December 3, 2026.
CABOMETYX TRx volume grew 15% in Q4 2025 versus Q4 2024, outpacing the oral TKI market basket growth rate of 7%, with TRx market share increasing from 43% to 46%.

Top line results from STELLAR-304, the pivotal trial of zanzalintinib plus nivolumab versus sunitinib in non-clear cell RCC, are expected around mid-2026 and could lead to a second NDA filing for zanzalintinib.
Full year 2025 revenue was $203.7 million, representing over 340% growth year-over-year and falling within the company's original guidance range.
Contract backlog reached $1.3 billion as of December 31, 2025, representing 3x growth versus the prior year and 42% sequential growth from Q3.
