Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $9.8 million compared to a loss of $13.4 million in the prior year quarter.
The company closed a $300 million non-dilutive preferred equity fund with OIC, enabling $1 billion to $1.2 billion of total CapEx for Asset Vault projects.

The company completed a $150 million convertible senior notes offering in February 2026, upsized from $125 million, with proceeds partly used to repay $45 million in higher-cost debt and a capped call resulting in an implied conversion price of $8.12 per share.
Contracted megawatts grew to 540 MW, expected to deliver $130 million to $150 million in EBITDA over the next 18 to 36 months.

The Calistoga and Cross Trails Asset Vault projects are operational and expected to generate $10 million in annualized recurring adjusted EBITDA, with Asset Vault Fund 1 expected to scale to $100 million to $150 million in recurring adjusted EBITDA by year-end 2029.
The company's developed pipeline exceeds $3 billion associated with 1.8 gigawatts of capacity, and it targets over 3 gigawatts and $1.5 billion-plus in EBITDA by 2030.
Iridium grew full year 2025 operational EBITDA 5% year-over-year to $495.3 million and generated pro forma free cash flow of $296 million.

Commercial IoT revenue grew 11% in Q4 2025, with more than 30 new IoT products certified and approximately 40 new partners added during the year.

Broadband revenue declined 10% for full year 2025 due to migration from primary to companion/backup plans, and the company expects the decline rate to moderate in 2026 partly due to a replacement opportunity across an estimated 130,000-140,000 legacy Inmarsat C terminals.

Iridium closed 2025 with net leverage of 3.4x OEBITDA and expects to delever to approximately 3x by year-end 2026, with a long-term goal of below 2x, and maintains a cumulative free cash flow outlook of $1.5 billion to $1.8 billion through 2030.

Iridium retired approximately 6.8 million shares at an average price of $27.07 in 2025 but has paused its share repurchase program, while the company expects the Board to again approve a dividend increase in 2026 following an average 5% annual increase since 2023.

Adjusted net income rose approximately 40% year-over-year to $16 million, with diluted adjusted EPS of $0.48 and adjusted return on average equity of 14.1%.

Baleen generated over $11 million ($11.4M) in premiums, more than 3x the prior year, with new business submissions up over 140%, quotes up over 110%, binds up over 260%, and a new business quote ratio above 75%.

Pre-tax net investment income grew approximately 44% year-over-year to $18 million, with a 4.6% book yield, 4.7% new money rate, AA- average credit quality, and duration extending from 3.0 to 3.2 years, targeting closer to 4 years by year-end.

Total equity ended the quarter at $459 million, with diluted book value per share of $13.80, and IBNR represented 91% of total reserves with only ~$600,000 of prior accident year reserve continuation, attributed to timing of premium billing rather than adverse development.

CoreWeave generated more than $5.1 billion of revenue in fiscal year 2025, up 168% year-over-year, making it the fastest cloud in history to reach $5 billion in annual revenue.

The company expects 2026 CapEx of $30 billion to $35 billion, more than double the $14.9 billion spent in 2025, with substantially all of it tied to already signed customer contracts.

CoreWeave expects to exit 2027 with more than $30 billion of annualized run rate revenue, up from the $17 billion to $19 billion annualized run rate expected at the exit of 2026.

The weighted average interest rate declined by 300 basis points during 2025 (nearly 600 basis points since 2023), representing nearly $700 million in annualized interest savings based on Q4 debt balance.
Average contract length increased from roughly 4 years to roughly 5 years as customers commit foundational AI workloads for longer periods.
Active power reached more than 850 megawatts across 43 data centers at year-end 2025, with the company expecting to double active power capacity to more than 1.7 gigawatts by year-end 2026.

Approximately 80% of CoreWeave Cloud customers paying at least $1 million per year have adopted one or more storage products, and the number of customers committed to spending at least $1 million grew by nearly 150% in 2025.

Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $898 million with a 57% margin, while Q4 net loss was $452 million driven by $388 million in interest expense, and Q1 2026 margins are expected to trough near zero before expanding to low double digits by Q4 2026.
Free cash flow increased 45% year-over-year to $4.9 billion in Q3 2025, with year-to-date free cash flow reaching $14.9 billion.
Wireless net additions hit a record 414,000 in Q3, with total wireless lines approaching 9 million and penetration surpassing 14% of the broadband base.

Broadband subscribers declined 104,000 in the quarter amid an intensely competitive environment.
Theme parks revenue grew 19% and EBITDA grew 13% year-over-year, benefiting from the first full quarter of Epic Universe.
Peacock losses improved by nearly $220 million year-over-year to just over $200 million in Q3, while Peacock subscribers remained flat following a $3 in-quarter price increase.

The company returned $2.8 billion to shareholders in Q3, including $1.5 billion in share repurchases and $1.2 billion in dividends, contributing to a mid-single-digit year-over-year decline in share count.
Broadband ARPU growth decelerated to 2.6% in Q3, with management expecting ARPU growth to step down more than 1 point in Q4 and continued pressure in early 2026.
Nearly 40% of new broadband connects chose gig-plus speeds in Q3, up approximately 10 percentage points from the start of the year.
Management stated the current plan is to not take a broadband rate increase in early 2026, focusing instead on transitioning customers to new simplified pricing packages.
Graham delivered record fiscal 2026 revenue of $245 million (up 17%), record orders of $359 million, and a record backlog of $533 million, up 29% year-over-year, with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.5x.

Graham received a $50 million strategic investment from accounts advised by T. Rowe Price (based on the 20-day average closing price as of April 13, 2026), used $13 million to repay debt, and now has over $100 million of available liquidity for organic and inorganic growth.

FLAC Tech, acquired at the end of January, contributed $2.8 million to Q4 sales, currently operates at a ~10% adjusted EBITDA margin, and was burdened by purchase accounting amortization expected to decline going forward.

Defense revenue grew 21% in fiscal 2026, driven by new program wins (including the competitively won Columbia-class submarine air turbine pump) and ramps on directed energy laser and 360-degree radar cooling programs.
Space orders surged 132% year-over-year as customers transition from development/qualification to higher-rate production across launch providers, satellites, lunar landers, and astronaut backpacks.
Fiscal 2027 capex is guided to $18-$22 million (including a new 30,000 sq ft Arvada, Colorado facility), with all strategic investments targeted to exceed the company's 20% ROIC hurdle rate.
Q4 2025 loan originations grew 40% year-over-year to $2.6 billion, with full-year originations growing 33% to nearly $10 billion.
Return on tangible common equity more than tripled to nearly 12% in Q4, with full-year ROTCE of 10.2%.
Full-year 2025 diluted earnings per share more than doubled, growing 158% year-over-year to $1.16.
Net interest income increased 14% year-over-year to $163 million, reaching an all-time high, with net interest margin of 6%, up 56 basis points year-over-year.
LendingClub's credit performance is 40% to 50% better than its competitive set, with net charge-off ratio down 80 basis points year-over-year.
Full-year 2026 guidance projects loan originations of $11.6 billion to $12.6 billion (21% to 31% year-over-year growth) and diluted EPS of $1.65 to $1.80 (42% to 55% year-over-year growth).
The company initiated its first direct forward flow agreement with a top U.S. insurance company in Q4, adding to previously announced agreements with BlackRock and Blue Owl.
Total deposits reached $9.8 billion, up 8% year-over-year, while total assets grew to $11.6 billion, up 9% year-over-year.
Under the $100 million share repurchase program announced in November, the company deployed approximately $12 million in Q4 at an average share price of $17.65.
The company is entering the $0.5 trillion home improvement financing market, with technology acquisition completed and first distribution partnership signed, targeting a mid-year 2026 launch.
Q1 2026 total revenue reached $184 million, up 43% on a spot basis and 37% FX-neutral, including 7 points of organic contribution from Sertifi.
Adjusted EBITDA was $39 million with a 21.4% margin, expanding 452 basis points year-over-year and exceeding the upper end of guidance.

Adjusted gross margin was 60.1%, down approximately 400 basis points, primarily driven by ~250 bps from Cleveland Clinic and B2B invoice client payment revenue mix, with the remainder from vertical mix shifts.

Flywire raised full-year 2026 guidance to 18%-24% FX-neutral revenue growth and ~175-375 bps of EBITDA margin expansion (reaching ~22.8% at the midpoint), with free cash flow conversion of 70%-75% of adjusted EBITDA.

The company announced an accelerated share repurchase program of up to $50 million, the largest single capital return action in its public company history, bringing total buybacks since launch to $128 million.
Education revenue outside the Big 4 markets (U.S., U.K., Canada, Australia) grew over 40% year-over-year in Q1, with more than 60% of new education clients signed coming from outside those markets.
Cornell University signed a long-term agreement for Flywire's full student financial software suite, and the company signed 3 additional U.K. SFS clients in the quarter.

Management estimates an additional $2.5 billion of payment volume opportunity exists within existing U.S. hospitality (Sertifi) clients alone, with international rollout to Europe and Southeast Asia underway.

Q2 2026 guidance calls for 18%-24% FX-neutral revenue growth and ~75 bps EBITDA margin expansion, below the typical annual rate due to lapping Q1 2025 restructuring savings and deliberate investments in domestic, AI, and Sertifi globalization.

Macro assumptions remain prudent with U.S. student visas modeled down 30%, Canada down 10%, and U.K./Australia roughly flat, while AI is driving ~40% auto-resolution of customer inquiries and a 30% reduction in support handling time and cost per contact.
DT Midstream's 2025 adjusted EBITDA was $1.138 billion, a 17% increase over the prior year, exceeding the increased guidance midpoint.
The Pipeline segment grew 27% in 2025, increasing from 50% of DTM's business at the spin-off to 70% today, the highest among its peer group.
DTM updated its five-year organic project backlog by approximately 50% to $3.4 billion, with pipeline projects comprising approximately 75% of the backlog and roughly $1.6 billion already committed.

Vector pipeline closed a successful binding open season for an expansion to increase westbound capacity into Chicago by approximately 400 million cubic feet per day, with an expected Q4 2028 in-service date subject to owner approvals.

DTM sees an addressable opportunity of up to 13 Bcf per day and a pathway of 5 to 8 Bcf per day of potential incremental gas demand in the Upper Midwest, driven by approximately 35 gigawatts of coal plant retirements and approximately 50 gigawatts of announced utility large load opportunities.
The Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.88 per share, a 7.3% increase from the prior year, with a 2025 dividend coverage ratio of 2.6x versus the company's 2x floor commitment.
Year-end 2026 forecast leverage is 2.9x on-balance sheet and 3.5x proportional, and the company achieved investment-grade credit ratings across all three rating agencies in 2025.
CBRE raised full-year 2026 core EPS guidance to $7.60-$7.80 from prior $7.30-$7.60, implying more than 20% growth at the midpoint.

The three services segments (Advisory, BOE, Project Management) grew revenue 20% and operating profit nearly 30% in Q1, with Q1 EPS beating expectations by nearly 10% even excluding the pull-forward of data center land development profits.

Global property sales revenue accelerated to 39% growth (U.S. up 64%), and mortgage origination revenue rose 53%, with the Loan Servicing portfolio up 5% to more than $460 billion.
Global leasing revenue grew 18% (U.S. +21%), with U.S. industrial leasing up 24%, U.S. office leasing up 15%, and data center leasing revenue more than tripling year-over-year.
The new Critical Infrastructure Services line within BOE generated $1.7B revenue in 2025 and $580M in Q1, and is expected to grow in excess of 60% in 2026.
Infrastructure-related activities produced over $3B revenue in 2025 and nearly $950M in Q1 2026 across all four segments.

Trammell Crow has approximately $900M of embedded gains to be monetized over coming years, with a ~$30B in-process and pipeline portfolio concentrated in industrial, multifamily, and data center land.
CBRE repurchased nearly $540M of shares year-to-date at an average price in the high $140s (~$148), and expects 2026 free cash flow conversion near the high end of its 75%-85% target range.
Guidance now calls for Advisory high-teens SOP growth and BOE ~25% SOP growth (high-teens organic plus a cost reclassification), with approximately 40% of full-year EPS expected in the first half.
KLA delivered Q1 FY2026 revenue of $3.21 billion and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $8.81, both above guidance midpoints.
Advanced packaging related revenue is expected to exceed $925 million for calendar year 2025, up approximately 70% year-over-year.
Services revenue grew to $745 million in the September quarter, up 6% sequentially and 16% year-over-year.
Free cash flow in the September quarter was a record $1.066 billion, with trailing 12-month free cash flow of $3.9 billion and a 31% free cash flow margin.
KLA estimates the revenue impact from additional U.S. export controls on certain China customers to be approximately $300 million to $350 million through calendar year 2026.
The company expects China revenue to decline from 39% in September quarter to high 20s in December quarter, and further to mid-20s for calendar 2026.
December quarter guidance includes total revenue of $3.225 billion plus or minus $150 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $8.70 plus or minus $0.78.
For calendar 2026, management expects first half revenue to be roughly flat to modestly up versus second half 2025, with accelerating growth in second half 2026.
Gross margin was 62.5% in the September quarter, 50 basis points above guidance midpoint, driven by stronger product mix and manufacturing efficiencies.
KLA's internal estimates value the advanced packaging market at approximately $11 billion, with KLA's share of that market approaching 6%, up from about 1% just a few years ago.
Northrop Grumman achieved a book-to-bill ratio of 1.17x in Q3 2025, with organic revenue growth of 5% and international revenue growth of 32% year-over-year.
Q3 2025 segment operating margin increased 80 basis points to 12.3%, driving a 10% year-over-year increase in earnings per share to $7.67.
Free cash flow increased 72% year-over-year in Q3, with full year guidance representing 22% annual free cash flow growth at the midpoint.
The company revised full year 2025 revenue guidance down to $41.7 billion to $41.9 billion due to delayed timing on certain awards and programs.
Full year 2025 EPS guidance was increased by $0.65 to a range of $25.65 to $26.05.
Defense Systems sales grew 14% year-over-year in Q3 (19% organically), with segment margin improving to 11.4%.

Mission Systems operating income increased 32% in Q3 with segment operating margin rising nearly 300 basis points to 16.7%, driven by a $68 million favorable EAC adjustment in the restricted advanced microelectronics portfolio.
For 2026, management expects mid-single-digit organic sales growth across all four segments, segment operating margin in the low to mid-11% range, and free cash flow of $3.1 billion to $3.5 billion.

In preclinical DIO studies, nimacimab monotherapy produced approximately 14% vehicle-adjusted weight loss, while the APC arm and the mixed combination arm both produced additive weight loss beyond the 21-23% seen with GLP-1 agonists alone.

Full-year 2026 guidance was raised: revenue to $44.5–$45.5 billion (up $500M), adjusted EBITDA margin to 12–14% (up 1 point at both ends), and free cash flow to $6.5–$7.5 billion (up from $5.0–$5.5 billion).

Gas Power gigawatts under contract grew sequentially from 83 to 100 GW across ~90 customers in 24 countries, with backlog at 44 GW and slot reservation agreements rising to 56 GW; the company expects to book 10–15 GW in Q2 and end 2026 with at least 110 GW under contract.

First-half 2026 gas turbine orders are expected to be priced 10–20 points higher per kW than Q4 2025 orders, with April quarter-to-date power equipment orders already matching all of Q1 2026 in value.

Power segment EBITDA margin expanded 500 bps to 16.3% in Q1, with 25 gas turbines shipped (+32% YoY); full-year Power margin guidance was raised to 17–19% from 16–18%, and Q2 revenue growth is expected at 15–17%.
Electrification Q1 orders rose 86% to $7.1 billion (2.5x revenue), with data center orders of ~$2.4 billion exceeding all of full-year 2025, and segment EBITDA margin expanded 590 bps to 17.8%.

Electrification 2026 revenue guidance was raised to $14.0–$14.5 billion with margin lifted to 18–20%; Prolec contributed nearly $500 million of revenue at just over 20% EBITDA margin since the February close and is expected to deliver ~$3 billion of revenue in 2026.

Wind posted a $382 million EBITDA loss in Q1 on a 25% revenue decline, with full-year 2026 EBIT losses still expected around $400 million; only 30% of onshore turbine shipments occur in H1, and Q2 losses are guided to $200–$300 million.

The company deployed $5.3 billion to acquire the remaining 50% of Prolec, returned $1.4 billion to shareholders (including $1.3 billion in buybacks), generated ~$900 million pretax from dispositions, recognized $4.5 billion of M&A gains, and ended Q1 with ~$10.2 billion in cash while remaining below 1x gross leverage.
Q3 2025 worldwide revenue was $1.21 billion, representing 22% reported growth and 20% organic growth compared to Q3 2024.
Q3 2025 net income was $242.5 million or $0.61 per share, the highest quarterly earnings per share in company history.
The company raised full-year 2025 revenue guidance to a range of $4.630 billion to $4.650 billion, representing approximately 15% growth.
Stelo surpassed $100 million in revenue in its first 12 months on the market.
DexCom now has active coverage for nearly 6 million type 2 non-insulin lives, representing about half of the type 2 NIT commercial population in the U.S.
The company closed Q3 with greater than $3.3 billion of cash and cash equivalents, with free cash flow increasing the balance by nearly $400 million during the quarter.
DexCom plans to settle its upcoming $1.2 billion of convertible notes in cash.
Q3 2025 gross profit margin was 61.3%, down from 63.0% in Q3 2024, with full-year 2025 guidance lowered to approximately 61% due to higher-than-expected scrap rates.
Management indicated that the top end of their base case 2026 guidance range is probably slightly below current Street consensus estimates.
The G7 15-day system has secured reimbursement contracts with Medicare, every major commercial payer, and commercial DME partners at the same net price to DexCom.
Annualized recurring revenue (ARR) increased 49% year-over-year to an all-time high of $588 million in Q3 2025.
The Samsung smartphone arbitration was completed and valued at more than $1 billion over 8 years.
Q3 2025 revenue was $165 million, up 28% year-over-year and exceeding the top-end guidance of $159 million.
InterDigital now has 8 of the top 10 smartphone vendors and approximately 85% of the total smartphone market under license, up from about 50% a year ago.
Smartphone ARR increased 65% year-over-year to $491 million, approaching the midterm goal of $500 million by 2027.
Q3 adjusted EBITDA increased 62% year-over-year to $105 million with a margin of 64%, up 14 percentage points from the prior year.
Free cash flow was $381 million for Q3 and $425 million year-to-date, nearly doubling 2024 levels.
The company has returned more than $130 million in capital to shareholders year-to-date, including repurchasing more than $500 million of stock over the last 3+ years.
Total contract value for licenses signed since 2021 now exceeds $4 billion.
Full year 2025 non-GAAP diluted EPS is expected to be $14.57 to $14.83 based on existing contracts, with revenue guidance of $820 million to $824 million.

Q1 2026 total revenues were $246 million, an 87% year-over-year increase, with commercial revenue up over 42% driven by TRYNGOLZA and DAWNZERA, including approximately $95 million of milestone payments from partnerships.
Ionis raised its Olezarsen peak sales estimate from greater than $2 billion to greater than $3 billion, positioning it to become Ionis' first wholly owned multibillion-dollar medicine.

Olezarsen received FDA priority review for severe hypertriglyceridemia (sHTG) with a PDUFA date of June 30, 2026, and Zilganersen for Alexander's disease received priority review with a PDUFA date of September 22, 2026.

Ionis raised 2026 total revenue guidance to $875–$900 million (a $75 million increase) and improved its non-GAAP operating loss guidance to $425–$475 million, while maintaining its target of cash flow breakeven in 2028.
TRYNGOLZA delivered over $27 million in Q1 product sales, with full-year 2026 guidance of $100–$110 million, roughly flat versus 2025 due to a Q2 revenue decline from the April 1 price reset.
Effective April 1, Ionis reset TRYNGOLZA's annual WAC price to $40,000, which will apply to both FCS and the anticipated sHTG indication, to integrate Olezarsen into 2027 payer contracting cycles.

DAWNZERA generated $16 million in Q1, a 125% increase versus the prior quarter, with full-year 2026 guidance of $110–$120 million in a switch market where over 75% of U.S. HAE patients are currently on prophylactic treatment.
Ionis ended Q1 with approximately $1.9 billion in cash after using $633 million to repay its 0% convertible notes due April 1, and projects a year-end 2026 cash balance of greater than $1.6 billion.

The first patient was initiated in the Phase III program for Salanersen, triggering a $45 million milestone payment to be recognized in Q2 2026, with additional milestones eligible from Sapablursen, Bepirovirsen, and Pelacarsen.

Bepirovirsen received FDA Breakthrough Therapy designation and priority review with a PDUFA date of October 26, 2026, with GSK expected to launch in the U.S. and Japan this year, contributing to five expected partner-led launches by end of 2027.
Farmer Mac achieved record net effective spread of $97.8 million and core earnings of $49.6 million in Q3 2025.
Total outstanding business volume surpassed $31.1 billion as of quarter end, with $500 million of net new business volume added in the quarter.
Year-to-date net effective spread reached $281 million and core earnings reached $143 million, reflecting double-digit year-over-year growth.
Infrastructure finance line of business grew by $600 million in the quarter to $11 billion, driven by data centers, broadband expansion, and renewable energy projects.
The Renewable Energy segment more than doubled year-over-year to $2.3 billion, and the Broadband Infrastructure segment doubled year-over-year to $1.3 billion.
Core capital increased by $131 million to $1.7 billion, exceeding statutory requirements by $723 million or 75%, supported by a $100 million Series H preferred stock issuance in August.
Tier 1 capital ratio improved to 13.9% from 13.6% last quarter despite strong asset growth.
The company recorded a $7.4 million net provision to total allowance and a $4.4 million charge-off related to 3 loans, partially offset by a $2.2 million recovery.
Farmer Mac reported a core return on equity of 17% while maintaining an efficiency ratio below the 30% strategic target.
Subsequent to quarter-end, Farmer Mac repurchased approximately 30,000 shares of Class C common stock for approximately $5 million.
Full year 2025 delivered 11% revenue growth, 16% adjusted EPS growth, and 290 basis points of positive operating leverage.
Average loans grew 14.4% year-over-year, with organic loan growth of $10.1 billion exceeding the $9.5 billion added through the Veritex partnership.
Fourth quarter adjusted EPS was $0.37, up 9% year-over-year, while GAAP EPS was $0.30.
Net interest margin was 3.15% for Q4, up 2 basis points sequentially, with net interest income growing over 14% year-over-year.
For 2026, standalone guidance includes net interest income growth of 10% to 13%, loan growth of 11% to 12%, and deposit growth of 8% to 9%.
Cadence is expected to contribute approximately $1.85 billion to $1.9 billion in net interest income and approximately $300 million in fee revenue in 2026.
Core expenses are expected to grow 10% to 11% in 2026, with Cadence adding approximately $1.1 billion to the expense base.
Net charge-offs were 24 basis points in Q4, with 2026 guidance between 25 and 35 basis points, likely at the lower end.
Tangible book value grew 19% year-over-year while the company returned 40% of earnings through dividends.
Management expects to add approximately $50 million per quarter of share repurchases in 2026 following the close of the Cadence partnership.

Q3 fiscal '26 recurring and other revenue grew 11.6% year-over-year to $469.9 million, beating the high end of guidance by $7.4 million, while total revenue was up 10.5% and exceeded the top end of total revenue guidance by $10.3 million.

Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 was $220.2 million at a 43.8% margin, exceeding the top end of guidance by $16.2 million, with adjusted EBITDA margin excluding interest income on client funds up 110 basis points year-over-year.

Paylocity raised fiscal '26 guidance, with recurring and other revenue now expected at $1.638–$1.643 billion (11–12% growth), total revenue at $1.755–$1.760 billion (~10% growth), and adjusted EBITDA at $638–$642 million.

Q4 fiscal '26 guidance calls for recurring and other revenue of $402.2–$407.2 million (9–10% growth) and adjusted EBITDA of $128.6–$132.6 million, implying potential year-over-year margin compression as the company reinvests in R&D and automation.

The company repurchased approximately 440,000 shares at an average price of $113.20 for ~$50 million in Q3, bringing fiscal year-to-date repurchases to ~2.3 million shares at $153.10 average price (~$350 million), and the Board authorized an additional $1 billion repurchase plan in April.

Paylocity announced the acquisition of Grayscale, an AI-powered recruiting automation company, expected to be monetized as a premium SKU after roughly a 12-month integration period, with immaterial near-term impact on revenue and EBITDA.
The company launched Paylocity Elevate Solutions, a managed services offering for implementation, payroll, and HR aimed at TAM and revenue expansion with no expected incremental margin headwind.
Channel referrals, primarily from benefit brokers and financial advisers, represented more than 25% of new business in Q3, continuing as a key growth driver.

Cash provided by operating activities increased 27% in the first nine months of fiscal '26, free cash flow grew 25.4% over the trailing 12 months, and free cash flow margin exceeded 24% on an LTM basis.

Average daily client fund balance was $3.8 billion in Q3, with Q4 estimated at ~$3.2 billion at a ~330 bps yield (~$26.2 million interest income), and full-year client fund interest income estimated at ~$117 million with no further Fed cuts assumed.
Q1 FY2026 total revenue was a record $285.9 million, exceeding the company's outlook.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q1 was $20.5 million with adjusted net income of $13.1 million or $0.22 per share.
The Board of Directors authorized a new $40 million share repurchase program after exhausting the previous program with $7 million repurchased in Q1 and $10 million subsequent to quarter end.
Auto insurance revenue grew 16% sequentially versus the June quarter and 4% year-over-year.
Home services revenue grew 15% year-over-year to a record $78.4 million, representing 27% of Q1 revenue.
Full fiscal year 2026 revenue is expected to grow at least 10% year-over-year and adjusted EBITDA at least 20% year-over-year.
Auto insurance margins are expected to expand 5 points this fiscal year and have already improved over 2 points since July.
QRP product grew 294% last year and is expected to grow at least 70% this fiscal year, while the 360 finance product is expected to grow at even faster rates.
The company doubled revenue from approximately $600 million to $1.2 billion over the past two years while only adding 26 employees (from 902 to 928).
Q2 FY2026 guidance is for revenue between $270 million and $280 million and adjusted EBITDA between $19 million and $20 million, reflecting typical December quarter seasonality.
GameSquare reported $5.9 million in net income from continuing operations in Q3 2025, compared to a net loss of $3.9 million in the same period a year ago.
Gross margin for Q3 2025 expanded to 49.4%, up from 15.3% in Q2 2025 (which included Frankly Media).
Pro forma adjusted EBITDA loss improved to approximately $200,000 in Q3, compared to a loss of $3.5 million in Q2 2025.
Q3 2025 total revenue was $11.3 million, a 22% year-over-year increase from $9.3 million in the prior year period.
The company held 15,618 ETH with an original cost basis of $55.5 million and an unrealized gain of $9.3 million at the end of Q3 2025.
The digital asset treasury strategy generated over $600,000 of yield in the last two months of Q3 2025.
At September 30, 2025, the company had approximately $82 million of cash and digital assets with no debt outstanding.
The company repurchased 833,124 shares at an average price of approximately $0.72, with $4.4 million remaining under its current buyback authorization.
Click Management is expected to contribute $14.5 million of annualized pro forma revenue and approximately $1.2 million of annualized pro forma EBITDA for the second half of 2025.
For 2026, the company expects over 20% annual organic revenue growth while targeting high single-digit to low double-digit adjusted annual EBITDA margins.
Q2 fiscal 2026 revenue of $665.5 million was a company record, representing over 65% year-over-year growth and non-GAAP operating margin increased by greater than 1,700 basis points year-over-year.
Q3 fiscal 2026 revenue guidance midpoint of $805 million represents an approximately 85% year-over-year increase.
OCS order backlog has surged well past $400 million, with the majority slated for shipment in the second half of calendar 2025.
The company secured an additional multi-hundred million dollar purchase order for ultra-high power lasers supporting CPO applications, with shipments expected in the first half of calendar 2027.
Q2 non-GAAP gross margin was 42.5%, up 310 basis points sequentially and 1,020 basis points year-on-year.
200-gig lane speed devices represented approximately 5% of unit volume but contributed roughly 10% of data center laser chip revenue, indicating a roughly 2:1 ASP premium.
The company delivered over half of its 40% indium phosphide capacity expansion target in Q2, ahead of the original three-quarter timeline.
Cloud transceiver revenue increased by approximately $50 million sequentially in Q2.
Management indicated the company is undershipping customer demand by approximately 25-30% due to supply-demand imbalance on EMLs.
Q3 non-GAAP EPS guidance of $2.15 to $2.35 compares to Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $1.67, with projected operating margin of 30% to 31%.
Playboy achieved its fourth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2025, with adjusted EBITDA of $7.1 million compared to a loss of $100,000 in Q4 2024.
Licensing generated over $46 million in revenue in fiscal year 2025, representing over 38% of total revenue at a 90% gross margin, with 90% of that revenue guaranteed through contractual commitments.

The UTG China partnership involves the sale of 50% of Playboy's China licensing business for $122 million in total cash—$45 million in purchase price, $67 million in guaranteed minimum distributions over 8 years, and $10 million in brand support payments.
Senior debt was reduced by nearly $58 million to approximately $160 million since Q3 2024, with an additional ~$52 million from the UTG transaction earmarked for further debt reduction.

Q4 2025 revenue increased to $34.9 million from $33.5 million in Q4 2024, while operating expenses excluding impairments decreased to $32.2 million from $37.9 million, reflecting a 15% reduction in selling and administrative expenses.
Net income improved to $3.6 million ($0.03 per share) in Q4 2025 compared to a net loss of $12.5 million ($0.15 per share) in Q4 2024.
Honey Birdette Q4 sales grew 9% year-over-year on a reported basis with full price sales up 21%, gross product margin expanded to 77.8% (up 140 basis points), and retail was up 17% like-for-like.
Honey Birdette implemented a 10% price increase around when tariffs went into effect with zero customer pushback, and Valentine's Day 2026 was the brand's best ever.
Playboy has over $343 million in unrecognized future licensing revenue and a $20 million annual minimum guaranteed digital licensing partnership with Byborg.
The Honey Club loyalty program launched in mid-October has already reached approximately 80,000 members, and digital sales grew 7% with average order value up 17% across all regions.
